paper.title: Generative models for pictures tiled by triangles
paper.abstract: The problem of generation of triangle-tiled pictures that are two-dimensional figures tiled by isosceles right triangles of the same size, is investigated. Grammars called context-free triangle-tiled picture grammars (CF-ttPG) that generate such figures making use of context-free type rules, are proposed. The special case that all rules of such a grammar are regular, is studied. In the framework of membrane computing which is a biologically inspired computability model, generation of triangle-tiled pictures by rules of a CF-ttPG is considered. The picture language of rectangular hollow frames which cannot be generated by any CF-ttPG, can be generated by a specific type of P system with two membranes.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Grammars and membrane-computing (P system) models that generate labelled pictures tiled by isosceles right triangles, and comparison of the generative power of the resulting language families (regular vs. context-free tt-picture grammars, P systems with two and three membranes, t-communication mode).
**Level:** 3 (Medium)
**Rationale:** The paper defines new generative devices and proves inclusion/separation results between language families, which is a substantive extension of array-grammar and array-P-system theory. It is not raised to Level 4 or 5: there are no complexity, decidability or universality results, and the proofs are short constructive or informal arguments rather than deep formal derivations. Following the instruction to default lower, Level 3 is assigned.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 7 numbered (tt-picture, rectangular tt-hollow-frame, CF-ttPG, regular rule, Reg-ttPG and language families, CF-ttPP, t-communicating ttPP), plus inline notions (adjacency, path, connectedness, background, derivation)
- Theorems: 4
- Proofs: 4
- Equations: a few set-theoretic expressions (background as (T1 ∪ T2) \ M, CF-ttPL = {L(G) : G is a CF-ttPG}, family inclusions)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 42
Expected range (Level 3): 10-40
Ratio: 1.05x upper bound

**Assessment:** Marginally elevated, but justified in kind. The grammar and P-system constructs are the objects about which the theorems are stated; the definitions are all used (Definition 2 in Theorems 2 and 4, Definitions 3-5 in Theorem 1, Definitions 6-7 in Theorems 3-4). The set notation describes genuine sets of tiles and language families, not programming lists, so no necessity-test failure is recorded.

### Issues
- The proofs are mostly informal. The negative half of Theorem 1 (no Reg-ttPG generates the T-shaped language) and the whole of Theorem 2 (no CF-ttPG generates tt-RHF) rest on intuitive arguments about a single growing head or lack of "control to stop" at a corner, without a pumping-style or structural argument. Theorem 2 also assumes "without loss of generality" that every derivation starts at the south-west corner, which is not justified for context-free rules whose left sides may contain several background tiles (the paper itself notes such rules introduce "certain context sensitivity").
- In the proof of Theorem 3 the rule assignment is inconsistent: membrane 1 is said to hold r1, r2 and membrane 2 r2, r4, r5, while the narrative applies r3 in membrane 1 and alternates r2/r4 in membrane 2. The language used in that proof is also called L1, the same name as the different language in Theorem 1.
- The closing remark of Section 5 refers to "Theorem 9", which does not exist (the result meant is Theorem 4); the Conclusion is numbered Section 5, duplicating the previous section number.
- Correctness of the constructions in Theorems 1, 3 and 4 rests on rule sets given only in figures, which are not available in the text extraction; they could not be checked.

---

## Citation Analysis

26 references. The first author appears in six of them ([6], [16], [19], [22], [23], [24]), giving an SCR of about 23%. None of the co-authors Venkat or Abdullah appears in the list; Wiederhold appears only as an editor of [24]. Every self-citation is topically close: [6] and [22]-[23] are the array P system and t-communication work this paper extends, [24] is the earlier triangle-tiled picture grammar paper whose definition is corrected here, and [16], [19] are directly relevant array/pattern grammar papers. No irrelevant self-citation is found. Reference [14] (a volume edited by Subramanian) is listed but never cited in the text. No citation ring pattern is visible.

---

## Structural Analysis

The claims are of a theoretical nature and each is attached to a theorem with a proof or a constructive example, so the claim-evidence balance is adequate, though weakened by the informality of the separation arguments. Limitations are acknowledged inline: the paper states that whether Reg-ttPPL(m) ⊆ CF-ttPPL(m) is proper "remains open", and that applications such as character recognition "remain to be explored". There is no dedicated limitations section. Prior work is positioned explicitly, including a correction of an error in the authors' earlier definition [24] and a comparison with the iso-array approach of [1], [2].

As a pure theory paper there is no code or data to release; nothing is linked or claimed (`relevant: false`).

The paper text contained no instructions addressed to a reviewer or an automated assessor.

---

## Conclusion

A conventional formal-language contribution: it introduces triangle-tiled picture grammars and P systems and establishes four generative-power results. The formal apparatus is proportionate in kind to the topic and only marginally above the expected count for Level 3, so no disqualifying flag applies. The main weaknesses are the informal proofs of the impossibility results, several internal inconsistencies (rule numbering in Theorem 3, a reference to a non-existent Theorem 9, duplicated section numbering), and a self-citation ratio in the elevated band, although every self-citation is relevant.
